payload.comment_body:
## Build Update

The assigned starting revision already contained the complete implementation in commit `74707bcf02f4b1ec1db823a3423111422eaecd60`: portable `Makefile` and native Windows `make.cmd` adapters expose aligned `worktree`, `typecheck`, `test`, `build`, and sequential fail-fast `quality` entry points. Worktree setup requires and quotes `FAKTORIAL_WORKTREE_PATH`, uses deterministic `npm ci`, and preserves npm failures.

Pages CI now runs `make quality` after its existing `npm ci`; artifact upload, deployment ordering, permissions, Node 20 configuration, package scripts, and application behavior remain unchanged. README documents both platform entry points. A hygiene follow-up in `c7c6a0a` removes two Faktorial result envelopes accidentally tracked by the prior build attempt.

Retained investigation baseline: npm installation, typecheck, 69 active Vitest files with 701 passing tests, and all three Vite entry builds passed on the clean pre-change head. Build-stage checks confirmed the GNU Make dry-run sequence, clean repository whitespace, and nonzero actionable failures for missing `FAKTORIAL_WORKTREE_PATH` and an unsupported Windows target. Per stage policy, full adapter quality/worktree execution was not pre-run and is requested from Faktorial's canonical verifier.

No Faktorial Runtime Notes, UI changes, generated assets, screenshots, ADRs, rules, material skill invocations, or custom proof obligations apply.

pull_request_description.delivered_outcome: The repository now provides one cross-platform Faktorial build contract for preparing fresh worktrees and verifying the shippable application, with matching Unix/macOS and Windows commands and the same quality gate used by Pages CI.
pull_request_description.implementation_approach: Added a portable `Makefile` and repository-root `make.cmd` with aligned worktree, typecheck, test, build, and quality targets. Worktree setup performs deterministic `npm ci` in the explicitly supplied quoted checkout path. Quality sequences typecheck, the complete Vitest command, and the three-entry Vite build with failure propagation. Pages invokes the portable gate, README documents both adapters, and mistakenly tracked orchestration result files were removed.
pull_request_description.solution_rationale: Thin adapters preserve the established npm scripts as the source of each operation while giving Faktorial, contributors, and CI a stable repository-owned orchestration boundary. This keeps application behavior and dependency versions untouched and makes setup and verification semantics explicit across platforms.
pull_request_description.tradeoffs_and_alternatives: A small amount of orchestration is duplicated between GNU Make and Windows batch so Faktorial can use a native repository-root adapter on Windows without requiring GNU Make. A new Node orchestration script was unnecessary because the existing npm commands already define the work. CI intentionally retains explicit `npm ci` before `make quality`, separating dependency installation from routine verification while the dedicated worktree target serves fresh checkouts.
pull_request_description.architectural_decisions:
The verification process now has a repository-owned cross-platform boundary shared by local contributors, Faktorial, and Pages CI; application architecture is unchanged.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  U[Unix and macOS contributors] --> M[Makefile quality]
  W[Windows contributors and Faktorial] --> C[make.cmd quality]
  P[Pages build job] --> M
  M --> Q[Typecheck then tests then production build]
  C --> Q
```
pull_request_description.verification: The retained clean-head baseline passed npm installation, typecheck, 69 active Vitest files with 701 passing tests, and all three Vite entry builds. Build-stage checks confirmed GNU Make target sequencing, clean diff whitespace, and nonzero Windows failures with clear guidance for missing worktree configuration and unknown targets. Canonical `run-quality` verification is requested and pending; it owns complete execution of the new adapters.

verification.reason: Commits 74707bc and c7c6a0a deliver the complete cross-platform adapter, CI/documentation alignment, and repository hygiene with clean static checks and verified Windows error behavior; canonical execution is required for final acceptance.
verification.handoff: If the gate fails, repair only the failing Makefile or make.cmd contract while preserving existing npm scripts, Node 20 Pages behavior, quoted FAKTORIAL_WORKTREE_PATH semantics, sequential typecheck-test-build ordering, and nonzero failure propagation.
